question: Which office of the union holds equity self-identification answers, who may read an individual answer and who only aggregates, what minimum group size suppresses a published count, how long an answer is kept and how Indigenous data governance (ownership, control, access, possession) is honoured?
decision: Equity self-identification remains disabled until a named union data steward, privacy impact assessment, participation/withdrawal process and applicable Indigenous data governance agreements are approved. Collect the minimum voluntary data, encrypt at rest/in transit, restrict raw answers to a narrowly authorized privacy function if any, publish only aggregates after minimum-cell and inference-risk suppression (starting threshold 10), and apply a jurisdiction/union-approved retention schedule. Do not promise both unconditional immediate deletion and fixed seven-year retention; do not treat OCAP as a universal agreement adopted for all Indigenous respondents.
originalProposedDecision: Implement exactly what the form already promises: the org names an equity data steward (default: none, so the feature stays off). Individual answers are encrypted and readable by no one in the app; only aggregates with at least 10 respondents per cell are shown. Withdrawal and deletion at any time; 7-year retention. Indigenous identity data follows OCAP: no use without the org's adopted OCAP agreement. Until a steward is named the feature is disabled.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
